column1: # Karagol ship cabins 074xx-076xx: travelers, rowers, Kaja, missing anchor charm, and the decision to sail.

column3: We should've hired guards\ndays ago. Now there's no\ntime to find anyone.{end_wait}
The captain won't leave\nwithout warriors aboard. He\nsays the Karagol is too{page_break}dangerous.{end_wait}
Surely there are fighters\namong the passengers. We\nonly need a few willing to{page_break}help.{end_wait}
They're paying well for\nguards. A man could earn a\ndecent purse on one{page_break}crossing.{end_wait}
There are things in that\nwater. Sending this ship\nout now feels like asking{page_break}for trouble.{end_wait}
If we turn back now,\neveryone will say Kaja was\nafraid. I won't let that{page_break}happen.{end_wait}
The longer we wait, the\nmore I worry we'll miss\nColosso. We bought these{page_break}tickets for a reason.{end_wait}
Silk Road is closed, so we\nhad to buy passage. I feel\nsorry for those who{page_break}couldn't afford it.{end_wait}
Look at the men belowdecks!\nThey pull the oars, don't\nthey? No wonder they're{page_break}built like that.{end_wait}
You're going to Colosso\ntoo? I've seen festivals\nbefore, but they say{page_break}nothing compares to Tolbi.{end_wait}
Perhaps we should go back.\nThis whole trip is turning\ninto a mess.{end_wait}
They know Silk Road is\nclosed, so they charge what\nthey like. What choice did{page_break}we have?{end_wait}
All those strong men rowing\nbelow! If the Colosso\nfighters look like that, I{page_break}can't wait.{end_wait}
We left Grandmother at\nhome. She'd make us spend\nthe whole festival looking{page_break}after her.{end_wait}
If we're not leaving soon,\nI'm getting off this ship.\nI'm tired of being told to{page_break}wait.{end_wait}
We're ready to row. Give\nthe order and we'll get\nthis ship moving.{end_wait}
Hear the drum? Every stroke\nfollows its beat. Lose the\nrhythm and the whole bench{page_break}suffers.{end_wait}
Rowing's hard work! That's\nwhat makes a strong sailor.{end_wait}
We pull the oars. Without\nus, this ship doesn't move\nan inch.{end_wait}
Once we're away from shore,\nleave the rowing to us. We\nknow our work.{end_wait}
You can't pull an oar\nforever. Make your money\nwhile your back can take{page_break}it.{end_wait}
I wish the captain would\nmake up his mind. We've\nbeen ready for hours.{end_wait}
When we reach Tolbi, I'm\ngoing straight to the\nmarket. I've had enough of{page_break}this hold.{end_wait}
They say there's an island\nin the Karagol. I've never\nseen it myself, and I've{page_break}crossed many times.{end_wait}
From the water, the coast\nnear Silk Road looks\ndrowned. I wouldn't try{page_break}that route now.{end_wait}
Enough waiting. If we're\ngoing, let's go!{end_wait}
When the oars hit together,\nit feels like the drum is\nmoving the whole ship.{end_wait}
The rowers try to outdo\neach other every voyage.\nSomeone always ends up with{page_break}sore arms.{end_wait}
See these arms? Years on an\noar will do that. Not much\nuse in a sword fight,{page_break}though.{end_wait}
We do our best to keep the\ncrossing smooth. The\npassengers rarely notice{page_break}how hard that is.{end_wait}
Save part of your pay while\nyou're young. You won't be\npulling oars when you're{page_break}old.{end_wait}
I don't like the feeling I\nhave about this crossing.\nThe water seems wrong{page_break}today.{end_wait}
Earn your money, then enjoy\nit while you're young.\nThat's what I say.{end_wait}
An island out there? I bet\nthere's something buried on\nit. There always is in{page_break}stories.{end_wait}
Want to see Tolbi? Then get\naboard. We can't sail with\nyou standing on the dock!{end_wait}
You want to bother the\ncaptain too? He's already\nhad enough visitors today.{end_now}
You're asking us to launch\nwithout the other ship?\nHave you spoken to the{page_break}captain?{end_wait}
My anchor charm is gone!\nI've taken it on every\nvoyage. I won't sail until{page_break}it's found.{end_wait}
We finally found guards,\nand now the captain won't\nleave without his charm.{page_break}Wonderful.{end_wait}
One missing trinket has\nstopped an entire ship. I\ncan hardly believe it.{end_wait}
I knew the captain was\ncareful. I didn't know he\nbelieved that charm could{page_break}keep us safe.{end_wait}
You came to ask the captain\nto sail, didn't you? He's\nin a terrible mood.{end_now}
If the ship from Tolbi had\narrived, perhaps I'd risk\nit. Without my anchor{page_break}charm? Never.{end_wait}
The captain says no charm,\nno voyage. We may as well\ncarry our bags ashore.{end_wait}
We're losing an entire day\nover a good-luck charm. Has\nanyone told the passengers?{end_wait}
It didn't walk off by\nitself. Someone must have\ntaken that anchor charm.{end_wait}
I doubt anyone stole it.\nIt'll turn up once we\nsearch the cabins properly.{end_wait}
If we don't sail soon, the\nfinals will start without\nus.{end_wait}
I hid the charm on top of\nthe mast. It was only a\njoke. Now I don't know how{page_break}to admit it.{end_wait}
My anchor charm! Where did\nyou find it?{end_wait}
We still have a long\ncrossing ahead. Keep your\neyes open. I don't want any{page_break}surprises.{end_wait}
The anchor charm is back.\nNow even the captain has\nstopped worrying. I wish I{page_break}could.{end_wait}
You agreed to help the\ncrew. When they need more\nhands on the oars, I expect{page_break}you to keep your word.{end_wait}
Those fighters look proud\nof themselves. Let's see\nhow they like pulling an{page_break}oar.{end_wait}
